final_candidates.decision_summary: Charge reversal in the catalytic domain could strongly disrupt activity. Its precise mechanistic effect is unverified, including whether it abolishes activity without compromising folding.
Removing the aspartate carboxylate could impair an important electrostatic interaction while preserving local geometry better than D223K. Substantial residual activity remains plausible.

Introducing an acidic residue into a locally hydrophobic catalytic-domain segment could disrupt packing and activity. Residue burial is unverified, and loss of activity could reflect nonspecific destabilization.

stop_reason.detail: Additional unsupported self-iteration is unlikely to resolve the mechanistic and folding uncertainties affecting the Top-3.

history.rationale: Charge reversal at an acidic residue in the catalytic domain could strongly disrupt catalytic electrostatics or local packing. Complete loss of activity remains a hypothesis without functional evidence.

The supplied sequence confirms D223; reversing its charge in the catalytic domain could strongly disrupt activity. Retain first place, but reduce confidence because neither its precise catalytic role nor complete activity abolition is established here.

Neutralizing this catalytic-domain acidic residue could impair activity while preserving its approximate side-chain geometry. This is a more structurally conservative alternative to D223K, but residual activity is plausible.

The supplied sequence confirms D223; replacing its carboxylate with an amide could impair an important electrostatic or catalytic interaction while better preserving local structure than charge reversal. Move above F257D to favor potentially function-selective disruption, although substantial residual activity remains plausible.

Replacing an aromatic residue in a hydrophobic catalytic-domain segment with an acidic side chain could severely impair local packing and enzyme activity. Destabilization rather than selective catalytic inactivation is a substantial risk.

The supplied sequence confirms F257 in a locally hydrophobic segment; introducing an acidic residue could disrupt catalytic-domain packing and reduce activity. Lower its rank because burial is unverified and any loss of activity could arise through nonspecific destabilization rather than a viable, folded inactive enzyme.
